news.2026-10-31-espagne-pib-inflation-t3: Spain grows another 0.6%, but inflation stays near 5%
The Spanish economy keeps growing faster than its neighbours, while energy prices keep inflation high.
Spain's GDP grew 0.6% in the third quarter, after 0.7% in the second, and 2.7% year on year [1][2].
Inflation stayed at 4.9% year on year in October, as in September, driven by energy and the war in the Middle East [1][3].
Key point: Spain remains one of the most dynamic economies in the euro area, far ahead of France (−0.1%) [1][2].
Inflation this high complicates the job of the European Central Bank, which sets a single rate for all euro countries [3].
If you travel or shop in Spain, prices there are rising faster than in France at the moment [1][3].
news.2026-10-31-allemagne-pib-t3-depense: Germany grows 0.2%, slightly better than expected, thanks to the state
Despite the energy shock and a record-low Rhine, the German economy is moving forward, carried by public spending.
German GDP grew 0.2% in the third quarter, when economists expected 0.1%, and 1.3% year on year [1][2].
Growth comes mainly from public spending; private-sector activity remains weak [1].
The economy held up despite the energy shock of the Iran war and record-low water levels on the Rhine, which hurt industry [2].
Key point: Europe's largest economy is not shrinking, but it depends heavily on state money [1].
The government expects 1.3% growth in 2026 and 1.1% in 2027 [1].
Germany is France's biggest customer: when it holds up, French exports benefit [1][2].
news.2026-10-31-portugal-logement-manife: Portugal: thousands rally for housing outside Parliament during the budget debate
House prices jumped almost 20% in a year; anger is growing as MPs debate the 2027 budget.
Thousands of people demonstrated outside the Portuguese Parliament in Lisbon on 27 October, during the first debate on the 2027 budget [1][2].
According to the national statistics institute, house prices rose by almost 20% between early 2025 and early 2026 [1].
Luís Montenegro's government highlights the wage rises planned in its budget [2].
Key point: housing is becoming the main social grievance in Portugal, as in several European countries [1].
The budget still has to be voted; pressure from the street weighs on the government's choices [1][2].
Lisbon attracts tourists and foreigners, which pushes up rents for residents: a debate that also exists in France [1].
news.2026-10-31-italie-croissance-nulle-: Italy stalls in Q3, with inflation at its highest in more than three years
Zero growth and rising energy prices: the euro area's third-largest economy is marking time.
According to Istat's first estimate, Italian GDP did not grow in the third quarter, slightly worse than expected; year on year it rose 0.8% [1][2].
Inflation reached 5.4% year on year in October, its highest level in more than three years, because of energy [2][3].
Key point: with Germany barely growing and France shrinking, the euro area is moving forward mainly thanks to Spain [1][2].
Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti is worried about the effect of wars on energy prices [2].
A stalled Italy means fewer orders for French companies, for which it is one of the biggest customers [1][2].
